characters.name: Oliver Wheatman
characters.description: Narrator and yeoman of the Hanyards; a country lad educated in Latin who becomes involved in the 1745 Jacobite campaign and later enters exile; central protagonist and first-person narrator.

characters.name: Katherine (Kate) Wheatman
characters.description: Oliver's younger sister; red-headed, lively, good-hearted country girl who tends household duties and inspires much of Oliver's early action.

characters.name: Mother (Wheatman)
characters.description: Oliver's widowed mother, kind, practical and a moral anchor of the Hanyards household; frequently comforts and counsels Oliver.

characters.name: Jane (servant)
characters.description: Servant at the Hanyards (dairy-maid and house help); resourceful, practical and a comic presence who aids Margaret's disguise.

characters.name: Joe Braggs (book)
characters.description: Local farmhand and poacher at the Hanyards; a wag and faithful companion to Oliver who discovers the great pike and rows Margaret on the river.

characters.name: Jack Dobson (book)
characters.description: Young cornet in Lord Brocton's regiment of dragoons; schoolfriend and rival in affection for Kate; a brave, boyish officer.

characters.name: Priscilla Dobson
characters.description: Jack Dobson's older sister; prim, formal and fashionable in manner.

characters.name: Master Dobson (father, book)
characters.description: Jack and Priscilla's father, a self-important townsman who entertains officers and others in his 'Ancient High House'.

characters.name: Lord Brocton (book)
characters.description: Ambitious, vain and predatory local noble; antagonist who arrests and maneuvers against Colonel Waynflete and his daughter.

characters.name: Earl of Ridgeley
characters.description: The Earl associated with Lord Brocton (his father); mentioned in connection with Colonel Waynflete and Brocton's connections.

characters.name: Major Tixall
characters.description: A petty, vindictive major often acting as Brocton's spy/agent; described as pimply and villainous.

characters.name: Sergeant Radford
characters.description: A drill-sergeant in Lord Brocton's regiment who conducts searches and questions at the Hanyards and later features in the dragoon party.

characters.name: Mistress Margaret Waynflete (book)
characters.description: Daughter of Colonel Christopher Waynflete; beautiful, educated, courageous and proud woman who becomes Oliver's lady in distress and key focus of his devotion.

characters.name: Colonel Christopher Waynflete (book)
characters.description: Soldier by profession and father of Margaret, formerly in Swedish service; arrested as a suspected Jacobite and central to Margaret's peril.

characters.name: John Freake (Master Freake, book)
characters.description: A wealthy, shrewd London merchant with wide resources and influence; a key ally to Margaret and Oliver and possessor of crucial papers.

characters.name: Samuel Nixon (Swift Nicks, book)
characters.description: Notorious highwayman referenced and later encountered; called 'Swift Nicks' and also 'Samuel Nixon' in the text.

characters.name: Martha Tonks ("Marry-me-quick")
characters.description: Ancient back-street woman, called 'Marry-me-quick' (Martha Tonks); a shrewd, kindly old woman who shelters Margaret at the 'Ring of Bells'.

characters.name: Sir Ralph Sneyd
characters.description: A local Staffordshire baronet mentioned among officers and gentry present at gatherings in the town.

characters.name: Sultan (horse, book)
characters.description: Colonel Waynflete's horse; called by name and fondly by Margaret and others.

characters.name: Master Bloggs
characters.description: The old grammar-schoolmaster of Oliver's youth who teaches him Virgil and Latin; referred to as 'old Bloggs' or 'Master Bloggs'.

characters.name: Lord George Murray
characters.description: Lord George Murray, chief military adviser to Prince Charles; voices the main military argument for withdrawing north.

characters.name: Prince Charles (Bonnie Prince Charlie)
characters.description: Charles Edward Stuart, the 'Prince' leading the Jacobite rising; charismatic but at times incautious and driven by hope.

characters.name: Sir James Blount (book)
characters.description: A gentleman with Jacobite sympathies who hosts in Exeter House; later reconciles private obligations with the political situation.

characters.name: Lord Ogilvie (Davie Ogilvie)
characters.description: Young Scottish noble devoted to his wife Ishbel; amiable and active in the Jacobite court and campaigns.

characters.name: Ishbel Ogilvie (Lady Ogilvie)
characters.description: Lady Ogilvie (Ishbel), a vivacious lady of fashion and friend to Margaret.

characters.name: Maclachlan (Captain Maclachlan)
characters.description: A young Highland chief and officer attached to the Prince's forces; ardent, brave, and enamoured of Margaret.

characters.name: Donald (Maclachlan's foster-brother, book)
characters.description: Maclachlan's foster-brother and a fierce Highlander; brave, devoted, and tragic — pivotal after Maclachlan's death.

characters.name: Lochiel
characters.description: A Highland chief present among the leaders; outspoken and influential.

characters.name: Marquess of Tiverton (book)
characters.description: The Marquess (Lord Tiverton), a courtly aristocrat in the Prince's company; social and urbane, favored by the Prince.

characters.name: Colonel Ker
characters.description: Colonel Ker, a Highland commander whose vanguard saved Margaret and Waynflete; a cooperating military leader.

characters.name: Colonel O'Sullivan
characters.description: An Irish officer and adviser who supports pressing on to London and argues for continued action.

characters.name: Sir Thomas Sheridan
characters.description: An Irish gentleman present in counsel; witty and involved in debate over military plans.

characters.name: Dot Gibson
characters.description: An agent/operative in Master Freake's employ used for local inquiries and actions; practical and resourceful.

characters.name: Jonadab Kilroot
characters.description: Master (captain) of the ship 'Merchant of London' that carries Oliver to America; a practical, blunt sea-captain.

characters.name: Peter Faneuil
characters.description: A wealthy Boston merchant who assists Oliver during his American exile; hospitable and influential in Boston society.

characters.name: Oliver Wheatman (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: Narrator and protagonist; yeoman returned from America (called Noll); central figure of the story.

characters.name: Margaret Waynflete (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: Narrator's love and later wife; the heiress (Miss Waynflete) and central female figure.

characters.name: Marquess of Tiverton (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: A marquess who courts Margaret; companion of the narrator; gambler and dramatist in society scenes.

characters.name: Lord Brocton (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: A nobleman and rival suitor; antagonist in a threatened public quarrel at White's.

characters.name: Sir Patrick Gee
characters.description: Coarse gambler and observer at White's who provokes and jeers during the challenge.

characters.name: Signor Zandra
characters.description: Italian teacher/assistant who aided the narrator in language matters.

characters.name: Master Freake (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: Wealthy nabob/merchant; father of the heiress and influential friend to the narrator; later partner in social ties.

characters.name: the nabobess
characters.description: Wife/mother figure associated with Master Freake; wealthy nabob's wife who later marries the Marquess.

characters.name: Sir James Blount (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: A baronet who brings news and features in household and social scenes.

characters.name: Lady Blount
characters.description: Wife of Sir James Blount; hostess at whose home narrator encounters Margaret and baby Blount.

characters.name: baby Blount
characters.description: Young child of the Blounts who playfully tugs at the narrator's hair.

characters.name: Jack Dobson (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: Friend of the narrator; formerly wounded soldier who recovers, marries Kate and later goes into business.

characters.name: Master Dobson (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: Father of Jack Dobson; business-minded and concerned with suitability for his son's marriage.

characters.name: Kate (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: Narrator's sister (often called 'our Kate'); affectionate, practical; marries Jack Dobson.

characters.name: Joe Braggs (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: Bailiff at the Hanyards; longtime servant and manager of the estate for the narrator; sometimes grumbling but loyal.

characters.name: Jane Braggs
characters.description: Wife of Joe Braggs or household woman; busy in the kitchen and part of family life.

characters.name: Mother (Wheatman family matriarch)
characters.description: Narrator's mother; matriarch present in household scenes and comforts the narrator.

characters.name: Archdeacon of Lichfield
characters.description: Once the local vicar at the Hanyards; gentle, fatherly cleric who later holds the title Archdeacon of Lichfield.

characters.name: the Colonel (friend)
characters.description: A Colonel and family friend who gives hearty approval at the narrator's marriage.

characters.name: Master Whatcot
characters.description: Craftsman who mounted the famous 'great jack' (taxidermied specimen); associated with angling lore in the house.

characters.name: Sultan (horse, The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: A horse referenced by the narrator (a mount he did not ride on one occasion).

characters.name: Swift Nicks (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: Figure appearing in the narrator's memory connected with a dead man and a bag of guineas (associated with past violence/theft).

characters.name: Donald (The Yeoman Adventurer)
characters.description: Companion mentioned among the dead (buried on Shap); part of narrator's wartime/earlier memories.

characters.name: Sim
characters.description: Acquaintance encountered on the couple's later journey; assisted to find a good match and business.

characters.name: Cherry-Cheeks
characters.description: Person met on the couple's journey (mentioned among those they visited).

characters.name: Nance Lousely
characters.description: A woman ('sweet Nance Lousely') whom the narrator and Margaret helped materially on their journey.

characters.name: Oliver (son of Oliver Wheatman)
characters.description: Narrator's son (a boy) who catches a 'little jack' fish in the household scene of the epilogue.

characters.name: Margaret (daughter of Oliver Wheatman)
characters.description: Narrator's young daughter ('my other Margaret'); cherished child present in household scenes.
